message.content:
I researched Apple and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812, versus a market of $222.70 bid / $222.72 ask — within ~0.15% of the quote and under the $10,000 per-order cap, leaving plenty of room in the $20,000 daily budget with no cash transferred out).

What drove the decision: Apple's official FY2024 fourth-quarter release (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year — a return to growth after a soft patch — and my verification against the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR confirmed full-year net sales of $391,035 million (up from $383,285 million), net income of $93,736 million, operating income of $123,216 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08. The modest dip in net income and EPS versus FY2023 ($96,995 million and $6.13) is explained by the one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge disclosed in the release, so underlying operating profitability was intact rather than deteriorating. News flow around the iPhone 16 cycle and the staged Apple Intelligence rollout was characterized as a "wait and see" overhang rather than a negative catalyst, which is consistent with a stock trading near $223 on ~36x trailing earnings — not cheap, but supported by a growing top line, ~31.5% operating margins and massive cash generation. I also disregarded one search result (stock-highlights.net) that misstated Apple's revenue and net income by three orders of magnitude ($391.0 million / $93.7 million) as clearly erroneous, relying only on Apple's newsroom and the SEC 10-K. Position sizing was deliberately a half-size starter tranche, since valuation leaves limited margin for error if holiday-quarter guidance or China demand disappoints.
